title: もしも～たら — if ever ～ (hypothetical)
summary: A stronger hypothetical than もし～たら. It is used for things that are unlikely to happen, imagined situations, or worst cases.

body.p: もしも宝くじが当たったら is hypothetical: winning is unlikely, but suppose it happened. もしも intensifies もし; the meaning is the same but it feels more unreal and speculative.
The main clause often expresses a wish or guess (～たい, ～だろう) or a request (～てください). It is also natural for precautions about a worst case: もしも道に迷ったら、聞いてください.

examples.ja: もしも宝（たから）くじが当（あ）たったら、家（いえ）を買（か）います。
examples.romaji: Moshimo takarakuji ga atattara, ie o kaimasu.
examples.tr: If I won the lottery, I'd buy a house.

examples.ja: もしも生（う）まれ変（か）わったら、鳥（とり）になって空（そら）を飛（と）びたい。
examples.romaji: Moshimo umarekawattara, tori ni natte sora o tobitai.
examples.tr: If I were ever reborn, I'd want to become a bird and fly through the sky.

examples.ja: もしも道（みち）に迷（まよ）ったら、係（かかり）の人（ひと）に聞（き）いてください。
examples.romaji: Moshimo michi ni mayottara, kakari no hito ni kiite kudasai.
examples.tr: If you ever get lost, please ask a staff member.

pitfalls: Do not use it for things that will certainly happen: もしも明日になったら is odd.
もしも only adds emphasis; the sentence shape is the same as もし～たら.
